speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an adolescent with a history suggestive of bone fragility, unusual physical features, and delayed menarche; can you tell me specifically what your bone fragility history involves, such as fractures from minor trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency) presenting with virilization and salt-wasting or non-classic forms causing growth failure and delayed puberty. The history of clitoromegaly, labial fusion, maternal hirsutism, and bone fragility (likely due to chronic hyperandrogenism/cortisol imbalance) is classic for this condition. REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone, Renal_Pelvis_ULtrasound, Pelvic_MRI.
